segments.text: Philosophy is the study of fundamental questions about knowledge, reality, morality, reasoning and human existence. FPSC’s syllabus is structured and thinker-based, so it can be prepared through comparison rather than memorizing biographies.

items.text: central problem → main claim → reasoning → key concept → criticism → comparison.
Avoid biography unless it explains the argument.
Use examples from ordinary life to explain abstract ideas.

segments.text: Prepare philosophy as arguments, not biographies. For every thinker or theory write the problem, main claim, reasoning, one example, one criticism and one comparison. This common template makes abstract topics much easier to retain and reproduce in examination answers.
